question: Can you upgrade a wastewater plant's switchgear?
html:
Yes. Electrical work at wastewater plants is a core focus for us, and Horton Electrical Services brings Connecticut wastewater relationships to CET (CET growth plan). Our data does not list completed switchgear jobs by name, so we would confirm scope, gear age and schedule at a site walk before quoting.

Who would do the work

  • Horton Electrical Services (Canton, CT) joined CET on Sep 15, 2026, adding 100+ field staff and 20 managers (CET public filings).
  • Combined headcount is about 260-290 people (est.), working from Worcester, Taunton and Norwell, MA, and Canton, CT (CET growth plan).
  • CET holds electrical licensing across six states (CET growth plan).
  • NuWave Energy Solutions adds efficiency work. This matters when gear upgrades coincide with high-load equipment such as aeration blowers (CET wastewater-plant targets).

Where plant electrical work is active

We track 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects across CT, MA and RI (CET growth plan). These are the leading ones:

PlantFlowProject on the books
New Haven East Shore STP40 MGD$82M wet-weather and odor-control upgrade on CT's FY27 fundable list, plus a $19.2M process-air-compressor request
Hartford WPCF60 MGD$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, fundable FY26-27, plus $31.6M in pump-station requests
Norwalk WPCF18 MGD$26M final-settling-tank upgrade, fundable FY27, plus a $48M aeration request
MWRA Deer Islandn/a$289M Clarifier #2 in the 2026 funding plan. The plant already generates 26% of its own power

(CET wastewater-plant targets)

Two caveats apply. In Connecticut, only Table 2 items are on the fundable list. Table 3 items are requests. Rhode Island figures come from a June 2026 draft list (CET wastewater-plant targets).

What we would need from you

  • Age and condition of existing switchgear and motor control centers
  • Whether the upgrade is standalone or part of a funded process project
  • One-line diagrams and any standby or self-generation tie-ins
  • Target outage windows. Plants run continuously, so phasing drives cost

Plant electrical work is the fastest route for CET to win Phase 1 business with Horton's Connecticut clients. It is also the entry point to SCADA and monitoring contracts, the recurring service mix that buyers price 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Pull Horton's past switchgear and MCC references at wastewater plants. That gives us a documented answer to this question.
  2. Check the electrical scope inside the New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk fundable projects. Confirm whether gear replacement is included or bid separately.
  3. Add a "switchgear and power distribution" line to the plant-target dataset so future answers can cite specific jobs.
  4. Draft a standard site-walk checklist covering gear age, outage windows and drawings for plant inquiries.
